title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Departure Board & Timetable. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Departure Board & Timetable
options.lineage: Swiss railway departure boards, enamel station signage and the printed Kursbuch timetable
options.thesis: Your stack as a station: releases are departures, and a service notice tells you whether your train still leaves on time.
options.viewport: Release page: a board row (Vite · 6.0.0 · date · Significance) under a full-width yellow service-notice plate 'Action required · 3 breaking changes', then key points and numbered changes.
options.risk: Pushed too literally it becomes a transit theme park; the grammar must stay rows, plates and footnotes, never trains.

raised.raise: Every breaking change carries a reference numeral that links to the exact passage in the original release notes, so nothing is claimed without its source.
State is never carried by colour alone: every Significance and Summary state owns a glyph and plate shape that survives greyscale.
What the Summary says and what the release notes say are visibly different registers, so readers always know what is quoted and what is summarised.

options.label: Compiler Diagnostic
options.thesis: Every release rendered as a compiler diagnostic: error[breaking], an arrow to what changed, help: how to migrate.
options.viewport: A diagnostic block per breaking change under a one-line verdict 'warning: action required (3)'.
options.risk: The most familiar look in dev tooling: close to every dark terminal-styled product in the category.

options.label: Lexicon Shoulder & Plate
options.thesis: Releases as entries ranked by apparatus, guide words naming the span you are reading.
options.viewport: A Release as a dictionary entry: headword, verdict in the shoulder, breaking changes as numbered senses.
options.case: Fuses well for reading long release notes; loses on audience identification and fights the dark default.
options.risk: Drifts into the bookish editorial look that reads slow for a two-minute check.

options.label: Emission-line Rail
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one rail; state is line form, not hue.
options.viewport: Releases as ticks on one calibrated rail.
options.case: Loses both axes: developers do not read state from line height.

options.label: Patent Drawing Sheet
options.thesis: A release exploded into numbered parts tied by leader lines.
options.viewport: Fig. 1: the release exploded into its changes.
options.case: Loses both axes: diagrams need illustration that release notes cannot supply.
options.risk: Decorative drawing with no data behind it.
options.kept: Reference numerals tying claims to their source.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.thesis: Releases as frames on a perforated rail.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link between editing film and upgrading code.
options.kept: Rank by grid span, not type size.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: Custody of an object told as one ribbon.
options.kept: Known versus inferred shown as different registers.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark developer-SaaS look (Linear, Vercel), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Header with verdict badge, card with key points, list of breaking changes.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
